reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows RTA-induced coercivity increases in FeCoNiMnCu and (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt thin films, but provides no data on equiatomic FeCoNi alone, nor on the formation of nanoscale ordered domains in that specific alloy. The key premises about FeCoNi ordering, anisotropy enhancement, and specific RTA parameters are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: RTA of FeCoNi-based alloys can induce nanoscale ordering that increases coercivity
Nanoscale ordered domains increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy and act as domain wall pinning centers
Equiatomic FeCoNi can form incipient ordered regions (B2 or L1₀-like) under RTA
The coercivity increase from RTA can be at least two-fold while retaining high saturation magnetization
RTA conditions (650 °C, 60 s) are sufficient to induce ordering without full phase separation in FeCoNi
